headline: High: AutoGPT can write files and use shell while MemMachine exposes MCP/REST, creating default-path prompt, data, and compliance risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: AutoGPT can read and write the filesystem and run shell/subprocesses, while MemMachine exposes an MCP Server and REST/Python SDK. That creates a plausible content-to-instructions bridge if MemMachine output is fed into AutoGPT, but the profiles do not prove a default direct channel. Uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF MemMachine outputs are copied into AutoGPT prompts or files without sanitization
IF an MCP tool returns attacker-controlled text that AutoGPT treats as instructions
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of MemMachine outputs into AutoGPT prompts
Add a fixed instruction prefix that ignores content inside retrieved text
Route MemMachine responses through a sanitizer that strips imperative language
Use separate workspaces for the two agents
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all retrieved content

B_data_leakage.rationale: MemMachine explicitly touches long-term user facts, preferences, and conversational context, and AutoGPT has filesystem and shell access plus allowlisted egress. If they share a workspace or AutoGPT reads MemMachine-managed files, sensitive context can leak into AutoGPT outputs or external calls. The profiles do not show a shared workspace by default, so this is medium.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same filesystem or exported conversation store
IF AutoGPT is given MemMachine context files containing user preferences or history
mitigations: Keep MemMachine data in a separate directory from AutoGPT
Restrict AutoGPT to a read-only view of non-sensitive inputs
Turn off exporting MemMachine context into shared files
Review allowlisted egress destinations before running both agents
requires-engineering: encrypt or tokenize sensitive context at rest

C_capability_conflict.rationale: AutoGPT can execute shell commands and spawn subprocesses, and MemMachine exposes API/MCP interfaces that may mutate shared state. The profiles do not prove overlapping write access to the same directory or lockless git state, but the combination makes concurrent mutation plausible. Because the shared mutable resource is not documented, uncertainty escalates to medium.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same workspace, cache, or database
IF MemMachine MCP tools and AutoGPT shell actions target the same mutable resource without locking
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate workspace
Serialize writes through a single orchestrator
Disable shell writes for AutoGPT during shared runs
Audit MCP tools for mutating operations
requires-engineering: add file/database locks around shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: MemMachine is a travel-planning agent with conversational context, and AutoGPT can act autonomously via shell and subprocesses. If AutoGPT-generated facts or plans are passed into MemMachine without verification, MemMachine may render or act on them as authoritative. The profiles do not show a mandatory verification step, so the cascade is plausible in default integrations.
conditions: IF AutoGPT outputs are used as source facts for MemMachine responses
IF MemMachine forwards AutoGPT-derived plans to users without independent validation
mitigations: Require a human review step before MemMachine uses AutoGPT output
Add schema validation for all AutoGPT-to-MemMachine handoffs
Mark AutoGPT output as untrusted in the prompt template
Compare critical facts against a second source before acting
requires-engineering: implement confidence and provenance checks

E_compliance.rationale: MemMachine touches long-term user facts and conversational context, while AutoGPT can egress data over allowlisted network paths. The profiles do not specify residency or retention regimes, so a compliance mismatch cannot be ruled out; uncertainty escalates to medium. This is primarily a MemMachine-plus-AutoGPT data-handling concern, not a single-agent violation.
conditions: IF MemMachine stores user history under a stricter retention or residency policy than AutoGPT exports
IF either agent logs conversational context containing regulated personal data
mitigations: Review retention settings for both agents
Disable verbose logging for sensitive sessions
Keep regulated data out of shared prompts and files
Confirm data residency for any external API calls
requires-engineering: align both systems to a single compliance policy
